title: DocuLink Document Values v1
description: Numbers, percentages, dates and printed reference data detected from text geometry on any document, financial or not. Every span is classified into exactly one of three categories: a value measures, a reference identifies, and noise is an artifact of setting the page. Values and references are click targets on every document; noise never is. Financial-statement structure -- notes, filing items and their citations -- is published separately in fs-structure-v1. Coordinates use normalized displayed-page, top-left-origin 0-1 space.

detectorVersion.description: Identifier of the detector that produced this model. Bumped whenever the published set changes materially, so a cached model built by an older detector can be recognized and rebuilt.

SpanId.description: Content-addressed span identity: a category prefix and a hash over the span's page index, normalized text and bounds rounded to three decimals. Stable across detector versions, which is what lets a workbook keep review state through a detector upgrade. NOT stable across a re-OCR that moves geometry -- a rebuilt geometry is a re-anchoring event, not an id-preserving one.

ValueSegment.description: One physical region of a span that wraps across lines or pages.

Value.description: A span that measures: a quantity, a proportion or a point in time. Always a click target.

normalizedValue.description: Exact canonical decimal for numbers and percentages, or ISO-like value for unambiguous dates. Never a binary float.

magnitude.description: Multiplier expressed by a modifier attached directly to this number. normalizedValue already includes this multiplier.

segments.description: Physical click regions when a logical value wraps across lines or pages. bounds remains the first segment; each segment creates the full logical value while drawing only its own rectangle.

Reference.description: A span that identifies rather than measures: an invoice or account number, a phone number, a citation naming a note or a filing item. Printed data a reader may want to capture, so it is a click target on every document -- an auditor sampling invoices captures the invoice number as readily as the amount. What a note or item citation resolves to is published in fs-structure-v1, keyed by this span's id.

kind.description: What the reference identifies. A new kind is added here before it is implemented.

segments.description: Physical click regions when a reference wraps across lines.

Noise.description: A span refused as neither a value nor a reference: an artifact of setting the page, or a token too damaged to read. Diagnostics only -- never a click target, and no consumer may treat one as data. A heading or contents row is not noise; it is structure, and is published in fs-structure-v1. What appears here for those is only the number inside one, refused so it cannot be mistaken for a value.

reason.description: Why the span was refused. A new reason is added here before it is implemented.

references.description: Reference spans on this page. Absent or empty when the page carries none.

noise.description: Spans this page refused. Absent or empty when nothing was refused.
